PURPOSE.statement: To author the narrow, bounded execution authority required BEFORE any Vercel environment mutation or redeployment, so that ONE coherent Preview deployment of the integration line can be produced and the FIBDB-053 D-1 state can be measured rather than assumed.
PURPOSE.what_this_artifact_is_not: It is not a deployment, not a configuration change, not an observation of any hosted system, and not a grant of any authority beyond the surfaces enumerated in DEPLOYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_BOUNDARY. The presence of a detailed plan here is not authority to execute it — the future execution lane is a separate lane with a separate freshness gate and a separate human confirmation.
PURPOSE.why_it_is_needed: See AUTHORITY_GAP_ADJUDICATED. Two frozen authorities describe the required end state and each explicitly declines to authorize the act that reaches it. The gap is real, not a misreading, and it is closed here by a grant scoped to exactly the act the rehearsal needs.

CONTROLLING_AUTHORITY.precedence: CLAUDE.md section 2. Nothing here supersedes a frozen artifact; where this artifact and a parent disagree, the parent controls and the execution lane STOPS.

CONSUMED_AUDIT_EVIDENCE.rule: The prior rehearsal audit is consumed as EVIDENCE, never as AUTHORITY. Its hosted observations are external to this repository and are NOT re-derived here, because re-deriving them would require reading hosted Vercel state, which this lane does not do. What IS re-derived is the repository half of every finding, so that no claim rests only on a previous report.

findings.repository_half_re_derived: origin/integration/commercial-v1 == 96a87611db0567e3399f9294113f96eab127771a at materialization, measured by git fetch origin --prune then git rev-parse. The SHA the audit names is the SHA the integration line currently carries.
findings.consequence: READY is an infrastructure state, not a health verdict. A deployment that built successfully and refuses every request at runtime is READY.

findings.finding: Runtime health = FAIL, with failure SUPABASE_AUTH_PROJECT_MISMATCH.
findings.repository_half_re_derived: SUPABASE_AUTH_PROJECT_MISMATCH is a real, reachable refusal code in this tree: lib/supabase/project-coherence.ts declares it in SupabaseCoherenceCode and raises it at step 4, when authIdentity.projectRef !== pin. The failure the audit reports is the failure this tree is written to produce, with the detail 'a self-consistent identity for the wrong project is still the wrong project'. It is raised BEFORE any Supabase client is constructed and before any socket is opened.
findings.consequence: The deployment is not partially working. assertSupabaseProjectCoherence throws ahead of client construction, so the failure is total for every path that constructs a Supabase client.

findings.finding: UELLIX_APP_ENV is absent for the integration/commercial-v1 scope.

ENV-10 and ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_CONTRACT.governed_vercel_staging_must_set both require the literal staging to be DECLARED, not inferred. An absent variable therefore fails the owner contract even in the case where the inference happens to land on staging.

AUTHORITY_GAP_ADJUDICATED.finding: REAL_GAP_CONFIRMED. Two frozen authorities describe the required end state and each explicitly declines to authorize reaching it. Neither omission is an oversight; both are written as deliberate refusals.

the_two_refusals.quoted: Deployment remains subject to the normal release process; this authority does not create a deployment permission, it removes the reason to withhold one.
the_two_refusals.reading: The runtime-first strategy makes deployment SAFE. It does not make it PERMITTED. The permission was explicitly deferred to the release process.

the_two_refusals.quoted: NO deployment to any environment is authorized.
the_two_refusals.reading: The release process itself, at its own materialization, withheld the permission. So 'subject to the normal release process' pointed at an authority that does not grant it either.

AUTHORITY_GAP_ADJUDICATED.conclusion: The permission exists nowhere. A lane that deployed on the strength of either artifact would be inferring an authority both artifacts deny. That is the silent authority expansion CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids, and it is why the prior audit correctly returned RELEASE_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED rather than proceeding.
AUTHORITY_GAP_ADJUDICATED.what_this_artifact_therefore_does: Creates the missing permission, and creates it at the narrowest scope that makes D-1 measurable — three branch-scoped Preview variables and exactly one deployment. It does not widen either parent, does not advance any gate, and does not touch production.
AUTHORITY_GAP_ADJUDICATED.what_this_artifact_therefore_must_not_be: It is NOT a general deployment permission, NOT a standing permission, and NOT transferable to another branch, another environment, another SHA or another lane. It is consumed by the single execution it describes and expires per EXPIRY.

GOVERNED_STAGING_TARGET_ADJUDICATION.question: May the governed staging execution target be a branch-scoped Vercel Preview deployment for integration/commercial-v1, identified by exact deployment id plus exact Git SHA, WITHOUT a custom domain or alias?
GOVERNED_STAGING_TARGET_ADJUDICATION.verdict: YES. A Preview deployment bound by exact SHA and exact deployment id IS the governed staging execution target under the effective authority. This interpretation is FROZEN by this artifact.
GOVERNED_STAGING_TARGET_ADJUDICATION.method: The three clauses that could have required a stable address were read for what they actually name as the target's identity. None names a domain, an alias, a hostname or a stable address. All three name a Preview deployment plus an identifier.

evidence.quoted: A Preview deployment satisfying S4, so that the journey exercises the certified SHA against the matching schema.
evidence.reading: The target is constituted as a Preview deployment. No address is mentioned.

evidence.quoted: The Preview deployment pointed at staging was built from the EXACT SHA whose migration corpus is applied to staging, confirmed by a build identity and a runtime identity endpoint that agree.
evidence.reading: Identity is a build identity plus a runtime identity endpoint. Both are reachable on a Preview deployment URL. Neither is a domain.

evidence.quoted: Every staging gate cites the exact SHA whose corpus was applied AND the exact target identifier. An observation that cannot name its target is not an observation of that target.
evidence.reading: The requirement is an IDENTIFIER, not an ADDRESS. A Vercel deployment id is an exact, immutable, non-reassignable identifier; a domain or alias is a mutable POINTER that can be repointed at another deployment without changing its own name. The deployment id is therefore the STRICTER identity, not a weaker substitute for a domain.

evidence.quoted: Every browser journey run is bound to the exact SHA that produced the Preview deployment it ran against, and to that deployment's identifier.
evidence.reading: Corroborates the same pair (SHA + deployment identifier) at the next stage, which is where a stable address would have been needed if the model required one.

GOVERNED_STAGING_TARGET_ADJUDICATION.negative_check: A search of the effective release authority for a required custom domain, alias, or stable staging hostname returns nothing. No clause conditions any staging gate on an address. The absence is not read as permission to invent one — it is read as the model identifying deployments by identifier, which the positive clauses above independently confirm.
GOVERNED_STAGING_TARGET_ADJUDICATION.no_alias_may_be_invented: This grant does NOT authorize creating, assigning, changing or removing any alias or domain. If a future lane believes the rehearsal needs a stable address, that is an owner decision and a separate grant, and it STOPS with STOP_FOR_OWNER_STAGING_TARGET_DECISION rather than creating one.

frozen_target_identity_form.rule: The target is named by BOTH of the following in every evidence artifact, always together, never one alone.
components: the exact Vercel deployment id of the deployment this grant authorizes
the exact Git commit SHA that deployment was built from
frozen_target_identity_form.why_both: A deployment id alone does not prove which code it carries to a reader who cannot query the platform. A SHA alone does not distinguish the authorized deployment from the failed one, which carries the SAME SHA — see BUILD_TIME_INVALIDATION. The pair is the minimum that identifies one deployment unambiguously.

mechanism.rule: The staging Auth correction is an ADDITIVE, NARROWER-SCOPE OVERRIDE. A new branch-scoped Preview row is created alongside the existing wider row; the existing row is not opened.
mechanism.platform_basis_verified: Verified against Vercel's published documentation at https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables (page last_updated 2026-09-17) rather than asserted from model memory. The documented rule, quoted: 'Any branch-specific variables will override other preview environment variables with the same name.' The same page states the override is additive in intent: 'you only need to add the values you wish to override.'
mechanism.why_this_mechanism_and_not_an_edit: Editing the shared row would change the value Production reads. Production is outside this grant, outside this lane's scope and outside the rehearsal's purpose. A configuration change whose blast radius includes production in order to fix staging is not a narrower fix — it is the widest possible one. The additive override changes the value for exactly one branch's Preview deployments and leaves the production-facing value byte-identical.

required_pre_mutation_verification.rule: MANDATORY. Performed read-only, BEFORE the human confirmation of HUMAN_CONFIRMATION, and recorded as pre-execution state for ROLLBACK.

This lane did NOT verify that the same precedence holds against a TEAM-LEVEL shared variable, and does not assert it. SECRET_CUSTODY_CONTRACT.classification: UELLIX_RUNTIME_DATABASE_URL IS SECRET-BEARING. It carries a database password.
SECRET_CUSTODY_CONTRACT.absolute_rule: Its VALUE is not contained in this artifact, must not be added to it by any successor citing it, and must not be written into any repository authority, manifest, evidence artifact, commit message, PR body, log line or test fixture.

provisioning.rule: The future execution lane consumes or provisions this variable THROUGH VERCEL'S OWN SECRET CONFIGURATION MECHANISM ONLY.
permitted: adding the value through the Vercel environment-variable interface or CLI, where the value is transmitted to the platform and encrypted at rest
marking it sensitive where the platform offers that classification
forbidden: writing the value to any file inside the repository working tree
writing the value into .env, .env.local or any tracked or untracked file under the repository root
passing the value as a shell argument that a process table or shell history would capture
echoing, printing, or including the value in any command output that is retained
provisioning.note_on_env_pull: vercel env pull writes real values to .env.local. It is NOT authorized by this grant. If a successor believes it needs it, that is a separate adjudication, not an implied convenience.

evidence_emission_allowlist.rule: Evidence about this variable emits ONLY the following derived, non-reversing facts.
permitted_fields: host class (for example: supabase direct, supavisor pooler)
forbidden_fields: any query string containing a credential
evidence_emission_allowlist.why_these_are_safe: Each permitted field is either public (project ref, port), a compile-time constant of this repository (the role name, per db/safety/database-role.ts, which db/runtime-identity-report.ts already returns to authenticated callers on purpose), or a boolean. None of them, alone or combined, reconstructs the credential.

local_inspection_protocol.when: ONLY if the execution lane must structurally parse the DSN to prove its project ref and role before provisioning it.
rules: a temporary scratch location OUTSIDE the repository working tree
no logging of the value at any verbosity
STRUCTURAL PARSE ONLY: derive project ref, role, host class, port and TLS posture; derive nothing else
delete the scratch artifact immediately after the parse

POSITIVE ABSENCE VERIFICATION: after deletion, affirmatively verify the artifact no longer exists and record that verification. Absence is asserted from a check, never from the fact that a delete command was issued
local_inspection_protocol.scratch_dir_hazard: The scratch location must not be inside the worktree even if gitignored. A scratch directory inside the worktree has been MEASURED in this programme to inflate ods:scope and redden the untracked arm.
local_inspection_protocol.on_any_doubt: If the lane cannot satisfy every rule above, it does not perform the local inspection. It provisions through the platform and proves identity from the runtime side instead.

SECRET_CUSTODY_CONTRACT.ssl_06_relationship: SECURITY_STOP_LINES SSL-06 requires an inventory recording who and what holds a privileged credential. This grant does NOT satisfy SSL-06 and does not claim to. The runtime role is least-privileged by design, not privileged, so SSL-06 is not engaged by this grant; if the lane finds itself holding an OPERATOR credential for any reason, SSL-06 is engaged and the lane STOPS.

PUBLIC_AUTH_URL_CONTRACT.classification: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is PUBLIC configuration. It is inlined into the browser bundle by construction and is not a secret. It is nevertheless SECURITY-RELEVANT, because it decides which project issues the verified subject that every row-level-security policy reads through auth.uid().

required_proof.rule: The future execution must prove MECHANICALLY — by structural derivation, never by eye and never by string comparison of a whole URL — that the project ref carried by the value equals the staging pin.
required_proof.why_both_directions: Equality to the staging pin already excludes the production ref. The explicit negative is stated anyway because the two refs have been CONFUSED IN THIS PROGRAMME BEFORE: db/hosted/target-identity.ts records that a July audit called ctaxtgujyyprgynmnvtq staging and that the dashboard settled it as PRODUCTION. A control that only asserts the positive would pass on a tree where the pin itself had been mis-set; asserting both makes the confusion detectable.
required_proof.derivation_authority: lib/supabase/project-identity.ts deriveSupabaseApiIdentity is the repository's one parser for an HTTPS Supabase API URL. The proof uses that derivation. It does not introduce a second parser, which is the drift db/safety/runtime-project-pins.ts exists to refuse.

the_current_incorrect_value.rule: The CURRENT incorrect value is NOT frozen here, NOT recorded here, and must NOT be preserved anywhere merely to compare against.
the_current_incorrect_value.why: Freezing a wrong value gives a successor something to restore. Recording it for comparison creates a second, stale answer to a question that has exactly one correct answer — the pin — which is already in tracked code. The comparison is against the PIN, not against history.

PUBLIC_AUTH_URL_CONTRACT.build_time_note: Because this value is inlined at build time (see BUILD_TIME_INVALIDATION), the value that matters is the one present AT BUILD, not the one present in the environment afterwards. Any proof taken from the running deployment must be taken from the deployment's own served output, not from the platform's current configuration state.

measured_behavior.statement: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is inlined at BUILD time.
measured_behavior.repository_evidence: lib/supabase/project-coherence.ts readInlinedAuthUrl documents the measurement against next@16.2.9: getDefineEnv spreads every NEXT_PUBLIC_* variable into the DefinePlugin map unconditionally, for the client, the Node server and the edge compilations alike, so a literal process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is replaced with a BUILD-TIME constant in all three bundles.

The guard therefore reads the inlined form and the factories consume decision.authUrl. One read, one validation, one destination.
measured_behavior.platform_corroboration: Independently corroborated at the platform layer by Vercel's published documentation (https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables, last_updated 2026-09-17), quoted: 'Any change you make to environment variables are not applied to previous deployments, they only apply to new deployments.' The repository measurement and the platform rule agree.

consequence.rule: Changing Vercel environment configuration does NOT rehabilitate the existing deployment. There is no configuration-only path to a healthy deployment.
consequence.therefore: Exactly ONE new build/redeployment is authorized after the configuration correction — see DEPLOYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_BOUNDARY.

BOUNDED_RETRY_RULE.default: A second deployment after a failed first attempt requires a FRESH ADJUDICATION. The default is STOP.

single_narrow_exception.rule: At most ONE retry is permitted, and only when ALL of the following hold conjunctively. Four of five satisfied is zero authority.
conditions: BR-1: the first attempt produced NO deployment that reached READY

BR-2: the failure is attributable to platform infrastructure (build machine error, registry or network timeout, platform-side internal error) and NOT to application code, NOT to configuration, and NOT to any coherence refusal
BR-3: NO environment variable was created, edited or deleted between the two attempts
BR-4: the exact Git SHA is byte-identical between the two attempts
BR-5: the human confirmation of HUMAN_CONFIRMATION is re-obtained for the retry
explicitly_not_transient: a build failure caused by a missing or malformed environment variable
any runtime 503 from a health endpoint
a deployment that reached READY and then failed health
single_narrow_exception.why_the_exception_is_this_narrow: A retry rule that admits configuration failures becomes a licence to iterate on production infrastructure until something works, which is exactly the unbounded redeployment this boundary forbids. A build machine dying is the only class of failure that carries no information about whether the configuration is correct.

EXPIRY.rule: This grant is consumed by the single execution it describes. It expires on the FIRST of: the authorized deployment reaching a terminal state (READY or ERROR) and its smoke observation completing; any STOP condition in FAILURE_ROLLBACK_CONTRACT firing; or the integration line advancing past the SHA frozen under AUTHORIZED_SHA_BINDING_RULE without the deployment having been triggered.
EXPIRY.after_expiry: No further Vercel mutation is authorized. A further act requires a successor authority.

AUTHORIZED_SHA_BINDING_RULE.rule: The deployment is bound to ONE exact Git commit SHA, frozen before mutation and re-verified immediately before the deployment is triggered.
procedure: SB-1: immediately before the pre-mutation human confirmation, run git fetch origin --prune and record SHA_FROZEN = the exact commit id of origin/integration/commercial-v1.
SB-2: SHA_FROZEN is stated verbatim in the human confirmation prompt. The human confirms that SHA, not a branch name.

SB-3: immediately before triggering the deployment, re-derive the exact commit id of origin/integration/commercial-v1. If it is not byte-identical to SHA_FROZEN, STOP_STALE. Do not deploy the newer SHA, and do not deploy the older one.

D1_PROOF_CONTRACT.rule: D-1 may be declared VERIFIED only when ALL EIGHT criteria below are measured ON THE SAME EXACT DEPLOYMENT. They are conjunctive. Seven of eight is not D-1.
D1_PROOF_CONTRACT.same_deployment_rule: Every criterion cites the SAME deployment id and the SAME Git SHA. A measurement taken against a different deployment, or against the platform's current configuration rather than the deployment's own behaviour, does not contribute to D-1.

criteria.criterion: Git SHA equals the authorized integration SHA.
criteria.measured_by: the platform's deployment metadata for the authorized deployment, compared byte-for-byte against SHA_FROZEN

the identity of the deployed SHA. D1-1 establishes which commit was built; the commit's tree is verified in the repository to contain db/stella/operation-tickets.ts NINE_ARGUMENT_COMPLETION_SIGNATURE and CompletionSignatureState. Bridge presence is a property of the SOURCE, proven in the repository, and bound to the deployment by D1-1.
criteria.explicit_limitation: No health endpoint reports bridge presence — see MEASUREMENT_GAPS_RECORDED.MG-2. D1-2 is therefore a source-plus-binding proof, not a runtime observation, and must be stated as such. It must NOT be claimed as a runtime observation.

criteria.criterion: UELLIX_APP_ENV is EXPLICITLY staging, not inferred.
criteria.measured_by: the branch-scoped binding's presence and literal value at build time, plus the deployment's own resolved environment
criteria.explicit_limitation: app/api/health/stella-preconditions reports the RESOLVED environment (via lib/stella/rate-limit.ts stellaRateLimitAttestation, which calls resolveEnvironmentDecision) but does NOT report the PROVENANCE field that distinguishes an explicit declaration from an inference. See MEASUREMENT_GAPS_RECORDED.MG-1. D1-3 is therefore proven by the CONJUNCTION of the configuration-side presence proof and the runtime-side resolved value; neither alone establishes it, and the endpoint alone establishes only the resolved value.

criteria.criterion: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL proves the staging project ref.
criteria.measured_by: structural derivation per PUBLIC_AUTH_URL_CONTRACT against the value the DEPLOYMENT carries, not against the platform's current configuration
criteria.note: Because the value is build-time inlined and public, it is observable in the deployment's own served client bundle. If Deployment Protection blocks unauthenticated asset access, the observation is taken under AUTH-4 instead.

criteria.criterion: UELLIX_RUNTIME_DATABASE_URL proves the SAME project ref and the intended least-privileged role.
criteria.measured_by: the deployment's own /api/health/runtime-identity response: runtime.currentUser and runtime.sessionUser give the role; verified:true with target.projectRefProven:true gives the project equality
criteria.why_the_ref_is_not_echoed: db/runtime-identity-report.ts deliberately omits the project ref from the payload and returns a boolean instead, documenting that naming it 'would put an infrastructure identifier in a response the safety layer keeps out of its own error messages'. The boolean is sufficient: verified:true requires targetFailures to be empty, which requires the proven identity to equal the expectation resolved from the environment. Combined with D1-3 fixing the environment to staging, this transitively proves the ref without echoing it.
criteria.role_and_rls: The same payload carries bypassesRls and isSuperuser. Both must be false. A role that can bypass row-level security is not least-privileged however it is named.

criteria.measured_by: the absence of SupabaseProjectCoherenceError on the request path. assertSupabaseProjectCoherence throws before any Supabase client is constructed, so any endpoint that serves a Supabase-backed response at all has passed it.
criteria.note: This is the criterion whose FAILURE produced SUPABASE_AUTH_PROJECT_MISMATCH in the prior audit. It is the single most direct signal that the binding correction worked.

criteria.criterion: Deployment health is green under the adjudicated smoke contract.
criteria.measured_by: the three health endpoints app/api/health/auth, app/api/health/runtime-identity, app/api/health/stella-preconditions
criteria.blocking_reason: RELEASE_GATE_LEDGER GATES[M11].measured_at_base records a blocking_contract_conflict: the auth endpoint is documented to answer 200 with an unauthenticated body for an anonymous caller, while production was observed answering 503, and 'either behaviour could be encoded as expected, so automating the smoke before adjudication would freeze an arbitrary choice'. There is therefore NO adjudicated smoke contract at AS_OF_BASE.
criteria.what_this_authority_does_about_it: NOTHING. It does not adjudicate the health contract, because doing so would freeze the arbitrary choice M11 refuses to freeze, and it would be authority expansion into a gate this lane does not own. D1-7 stays BLOCKED and D-1 stays undeclarable until a competent authority adjudicates the contract.
criteria.what_the_execution_lane_may_still_do: It may RECORD the observed responses verbatim (status codes and non-secret bodies) as raw evidence for the future adjudication. Recording an observation is not declaring a contract.

criteria.criterion: The hosted database is INDEPENDENTLY observed to be OLD_DB: the nine-argument signature ABSENT and the seven-argument signature PRESENT.
criteria.must_not_be_inferred: OLD_DB must NOT be inferred from repository state. The repository proves what the Stage-A package WOULD install, not what the hosted catalog CURRENTLY holds. Those are different propositions, and the gap between them is precisely the sequence risk that FAILURE_ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.new_db_unexpected exists to catch.
criteria.must_not_be_inferred_from_the_bridge_eit: The running bridge probes the catalog and selects a state, but its verdict is reached inside a governed Stella completion — a product mutation no part of this grant authorizes. A probe result obtained by exercising the product is not a read-only observation.

HOSTED_CATALOG_OBSERVATION_DISPOSITION.question: May THIS authority safely authorize a read-only catalog probe against the staging database, so that D1-8 becomes measurable?

grounds.ground: The parent release authority forecloses it by its own words. STAGING_RELEASE_PRODUCTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json EXPLICIT_NON_AUTHORIZATIONS states: 'NO hosted access of any kind was performed or is authorized by this artifact.' This artifact is a release-domain child. A child that granted hosted database access would be conferring, by inference, an authority its parent enumerated specifically so a successor could not read it in.

A hosted catalog probe requires an operator-class credential this grant does not hold and must not acquire. SECURITY_STOP_LINES SSL-06: 'No privileged credential may be held without an inventory recording who and what holds it.' Absorbing the probe would either engage SSL-06 or require this lane to create a custody inventory it has no authority to create.

A hosted staging observation already has a home and an evidence class. HOSTED_DDL_PRECONDITIONS HDP-1 names the STAGING_OBSERVATION_PACKET and binds it to gates S1, G12 and S9. Routing a second, differently-shaped observation through a Vercel-binding authority would create a second answer to a question that already has an owner — the drift the repository refuses elsewhere.

The hosted connection path is governed by a different contract. db/hosted/target-identity.ts requires three positive signals per invocation via verifyStagingTarget and records that KNOWN_STAGING_PROJECT_REF 'is NOT authority to connect'. That contract belongs to the hosted operator domain, not to the release-binding domain this artifact occupies.

HOSTED_CATALOG_OBSERVATION_DISPOSITION.not_absorbed_silently: Recorded explicitly, as required, rather than quietly folded in. A reader who expected this authority to cover the probe is told plainly that it does not.

shape_a_successor_authority_would_need.note: Recorded as a SPECIFICATION FOR A FUTURE AUTHORITY, not as a grant. Nothing here authorizes any of it.
scope: an exact target identity gate FIRST, before any query, per the three-positive-signal contract
no secret in any emitted evidence

the_two_literals_it_would_compare.source: FIBDB053_RUNTIME_COMPANION_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json SECTION_A3, quoted so a successor does not recompose them
the_two_literals_it_would_compare.fixed_literal_rule: Both are FIXED LITERALS. Never composed, never interpolated, never built from a variable holding a type name. A wrong signature resolves to NULL without raising, so a composed literal is silently indistinguishable from a legitimately absent function.
the_two_literals_it_would_compare.both_directions_required: Asserting only the nine-argument absence would pass against a database where the function does not exist at all, or where the schema is missing. The seven-argument presence is what makes the absence meaningful.

FAILURE_ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.general_rule: Every branch below is a STOP. None is a diagnosis to be worked around. The lane does not edit another variable opportunistically, and does not deploy again outside BOUNDED_RETRY_RULE.

branches.condition: The new deployment fails environment coherence (any SupabaseCoherenceCode raised).
branches.action: STOP. Record the code. Do not mutate any further variable.
branches.why: A coherence refusal means the three-way equality is unmet. Editing one more variable to see if it helps is guessing at a configuration whose correct state is fully specified; the specification is re-read, not probed.

branches.condition: The deployed SHA is correct but the database identity is wrong (SUPABASE_DB_PROJECT_MISMATCH, or a role that is not the intended least-privileged role).
branches.why: A correct build pointed at the wrong database is the worst of the failure modes: it looks healthy from the outside while reading and writing somewhere it must not.

branches.condition: Auth and database project identities disagree (SUPABASE_AUTH_DB_PROJECT_DIVERGENCE).
branches.why: Quoted from lib/supabase/project-coherence.ts: 'Sessions verified by one project would be used as row-level-security subjects in another.' The policies are not bypassed; they are evaluated correctly for a subject belonging to a different database.

branches.condition: The hosted database is already NEW_DB, unexpectedly.
rules: Do NOT attempt to restore a prior schema state.
Do NOT treat it as a happy accident that skips a step.

It also means the window between then and now was D-3 — the single PROHIBITED cell of DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT, described there as 'a total outage of the governed Stella completion path for every affected category'. That is an incident to adjudicate, not a state to build on.
